meta.heading: Round 10: Canvas step 1 is built
meta.intro: The Desk is now the Canvas, and the old Desk is Day. Real screenshots with sample data. Steps 2 to 5 (project areas, links, timeline; stacks and drawers; boards and the Archive; the meeting canvas) come next, in that order.

r10-c1.title: Built: the Desk is a canvas of your real work
body: Shiftbook now opens on the **Desk**: your entries, Done tickets, notes and Inbox scraps from the last week as paper cards. Drag a card anywhere and it stays there, even after the week is over. Drag empty paper or scroll to move around, Ctrl + scroll to zoom, and **Fit everything** brings it all into view.

**Double-click a card to open it:** an entry opens its details, a note opens in Notes, a scrap goes into Log work, and a Done ticket takes a few words right on the card. **Double-click empty paper to jot** something; Enter keeps it. **Right-click** any card for its paper menu, the same options as on Day.

The panel on the right has what you need while working: today's hours, Where was I?, Log work, Done tickets and the wrap-up. Anything you log appears as a card straight away. The **>** button folds the panel away.
**Day** (key 2) is the old Desk, for starting and ending the day. Keys 1 to 5 are now Desk, Day, Timesheet, Notes and Settings.

figures.caption: The Desk: cards on the left, the panel on the right. The cards in the middle were moved by hand; the rest were placed automatically.
Right-click an entry card: the same paper menu as on Day.
Double-click empty paper and type: a jot, kept where you wrote it.
Day: the structured view for starting and ending the day.

options.why: Say what to change in the note.

questions.legend: Entries and Done tickets leave the Desk after a week unless you moved them. Is a week right?

r10-c1.pick: Yes, keep going, with a week. Notes and scraps stay until you archive them, so nothing you wrote disappears.
r10-c1.reply: Thanks. A week it is. Building step 2 now: project areas, links and the timeline.
